growth_story.headline: After years of political crisis and frozen aid, Togo's income per person has grown steadily since 2008 and reached a new high in 2025.
growth_story.arc: Togo's income per person barely moved from 1990 to 1997, growing 0.5 percent a year: a political crisis from 1991 cut aid, and a steep fall in 1993 gave way to a short rebound after the 1994 devaluation. From 1998 to 2007 it shrank by 1.9 percent a year, as donors stayed away, Togo fell into arrears with the World Bank in 2002 and debt piled up. A 2006 political accord and 2007 elections brought partners back, debt relief followed in 2010, and growth turned positive from 2008. Since then income per person has grown 3.0 percent a year (2008 to 2025), helped by an expanded port at Lomé, trade and transport services and heavy public investment. Growth has also picked up within this era, to 3.0 percent a year over 2016 to 2025 against 1.8 in the decade before, and income per person reached its highest level yet in 2025.

threads.title: A decade of political crisis
threads.text: From 1991 Togo went through a long political crisis, and aid fell through 2002. Income per person dropped 14.1 percent in 1993. The 1994 devaluation of the CFA franc brought a short burst of growth, reaching 10.6 percent in 1997, that then faded.

threads.title: Arrears, then partners return
threads.text: In 2002 Togo could no longer pay its debts, and the World Bank joined other donors in halting support. Income per person fell in most years up to 2007, including by 7.0 percent in 2005. A 2006 political accord and 2007 elections brought partners back, and debt relief followed in 2010.

since_last_year.text: Income per person grew 4.0 percent in 2025, the fourth year in a row at 4.0 percent or more, led by services. Activity slowed in early 2026, and the World Bank expects growth to ease this year amid tighter budgets, weaker global demand and price pressures.

growth_story.tension: The sources describe a decade of robust growth, but a growing population absorbed much of it: income per person rose 3.0 percent a year over 2016 to 2025, and it passed its 1980 high only in 2021. A 2025 World Bank update also puts growth in income per person since the mid-2000s well below this data's 20-year average of 2.4; the sources do not explain the gap.
